(Boca Raton, Florida) | college = [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] (2021–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 45 | draft_team = [[Charlotte Hornets]] | career_start = 2022 | years1 = {{nbay|2022|start}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team1 = [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] | years2 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022]]–[[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team2 = →[[Iowa Wolves]] | years3 = {{nbay|2025|full=y}} | team3 = [[Boston Celtics]] | years4 = {{nbay|2025|end}}–present | team4 = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | years5 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]] | team5 = →[[Long Island Nets]] | highlights = * [[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] All-Freshman Team (2022) }} '''Joshua Robert Tyler Minott''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|m|aɪ|n|ɒ|t}} {{respell|MY|not}};{{cite press release |author= |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 18, 2024}} born November 25, 2002) is a Jamaican-American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]]. Minott was selected by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] with the 45th overall pick in the [[2022 NBA draft]], but was immediately traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. After spending his first three seasons with the Timberwolves, Minott signed with the [[Boston Celtics]] in July of 2025. Minott would play for the Celtics for half of the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]] before being traded to the Nets in February of 2026. ==Early life== Minott played basketball for [[Saint Andrew's School (Boca Raton, Florida)|Saint Andrew's School]] in [[Boca Raton, Florida]]. In his junior season, he averaged 17.2 points, 7.4 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game, helping his team win the Class 3A state championship, its first state title.{{cite web |last=Nelsen |first=Chris |title=HS boys basketball preview: St. Andrew's looks to go back-to-back; Forest Hill eyes state return; Wellington regroups |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2020/12/02/josh-minott-looks-lead-st-andrews-another-fhsaa-state-title/3795642001/ |website=[[The Palm Beach Post]] |access-date=June 14, 2022 |archive-date=December 2, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201202182426/https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2020/12/02/josh-minott-looks-lead-st-andrews-another-fhsaa-state-title/3795642001/?utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter_pbpsports |date=December 2, 2020}} As a senior, Minott averaged 23.1 points and 8.3 rebounds per game, and was named [[Palm Beach County, Florida|Palm Beach County]] Class 5A-1A Player of the Year by the ''[[Sun-Sentinel]]''.{{cite web |last=Lichtenstein |first=Adam |title=Palm Beach 5A-1A boys basketball player of the year: Joshua Minott, St. Andrew's senior |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/all-county/fl-sp-ss-prem-ac-pb-bhoop-small-poy-20210328-tqfinuojendjhiype6grxv4nmy-story.html |website=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=March 27, 2021}} A four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] over offers from [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] and [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]].{{cite web |last=Munz |first=Jason |title=4-star prospect Josh Minott commits to Memphis |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2020/08/08/memphis-basketball-josh-minott-penny-hardaway-recruiting-cody-toppert/5571709002/ |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=August 8, 2020}} ==College career== On January 23, 2022, Minott recorded a career-high 18 points and nine rebounds in an 83–81 win over [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa]].{{cite web |last=Munz |first=Jason |title=Memphis basketball rallies from 15-point deficit to beat Tulsa: Our top takeaways |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2022/01/23/memphis-basketball-tyler-harris-josh-minott-lead-tigers-win-tulsa/9063897002/ |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=January 23, 2022}} As a freshman at Memphis, he averaged 6.6 points and 3.8 rebounds in 14.6 minutes per game. Minott was named to the [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) All-Freshman Team and was a three-time AAC Freshman of the Week. On March 24, 2022, he declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Smarr |first=Emilee |title=Former St. Andrew's star Josh Minott declares for 2022 NBA draft |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2022/03/24/josh-minott-former-st-andrews-star-declares-2022-nba-draft/7154292001/ |website=[[The Palm Beach Post]] |access-date=June 14, 2022 |archive-date=March 24, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220324234749/https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2022/03/24/josh-minott-former-st-andrews-star-declares-2022-nba-draft/7154292001/?utm_campaign=snd-autopilot&utm_source=twitter&utm_medium=Social&utm_campaign=ghf-palmbeach-main |date=March 24, 2022}} He opted to remain in the draft, forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |title=Report: Memphis freshman Josh Minott to stay in NBA draft |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/05/27/memphis-josh-minott-nba-draft-agent/ |publisher=The Rookie Wire |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=May 27, 2022}} == Professional career == === Minnesota Timberwolves (2022–2025) === In the [[2022 NBA draft]], Minott was drafted by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] with the 45th pick in the draft. He was later traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], along with a 2023 second-round draft pick via the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for [[Bryce McGowens]], the 40th pick in the draft.{{Cite web |date=June 23, 2022 |title=Hornets Acquire Draft Rights To No. 40 Pick Bryce McGowens From Minnesota Timberwolves |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-acquire-draft-rights-to-no-40-pick-bryce-mcgowens-from-minnesota-timberwolves |access-date=2022-07-23 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} Minott joined the Timberwolves' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] roster.{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Timberwolves 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612750/timberwolves |access-date=2022-07-23 |website=NBA.com}} In his Summer League debut, Minott scored twenty-two points and had ten rebounds in a 85–78 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{Cite web |title=Denver Nuggets vs Minnesota Timberwolves Jul 8, 2022 Box Score |url=https://www.nba.com/game/den-vs-min-1522200008/box-score#box-score |access-date=2022-07-23 |website=NBA.com}} On July 17, 2022, Minott signed a four-year, $6.8 million deal with the Timberwolves.{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |date=2022-07-17 |title=Timberwolves to sign Memphis' Josh Minott to 4-year, $6.8M contract |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2022/07/17/timberwolves-josh-minott-rookie-contract/ |access-date=2022-07-23 |website=The Rookie Wire |language=en-US}} === Boston Celtics (2025–2026) === On July 7, 2025, Minott signed a two-year, $5 million contract with the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/070725-press-release-celtics-sign-luka-garza-and-josh-minott|title=Celtics Sign Luka Garza and Josh Minott|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2025}}{{cite web | last=Hill | first=Arthur | title=Celtics Sign Josh Minott To Two-Year Deal | website=Hoops Rumors | date=2025-07-01 | url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/07/celtics-josh-minott-agree-to-two-year-deal.html | access-date=2025-12-06}} === Brooklyn Nets (2026–present) === On February 5, 2026, Minott was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for cash considerations.{{Cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Acquire Josh Minott |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklynnetsacquirejoshminott |access-date=2026-02-06 |date=2026-02-05 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} On February 17, he and [[Ben Saraf]] were assigned to the [[Long Island Nets]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{Cite web |date=February 17, 2026 |title=Brooklyn Nets Assign Ben Saraf and Josh Minott to Long Island |url=https://x.com/LongIslandNets/status/2023873941794943030?s=20}} On March 12, Minott recorded a career-high 24 points during a 97–108 loss to the [[2025–26 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web|title=Nets' Josh Minott: Scores career-high 24 points|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/nets-josh-minott-scores-career-high-24-points/|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} He made 16 total appearances (including one start) for Brooklyn, recording averages of 10.8 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 0.8 assists. On June 29, 2026, Minott re-signed with the Nets on a two-year, $9 million contract.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=June 29, 2026 |title=Sources: Nets agree to 2-year deals with Sharpe, Minott |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49217954/sources-nets-agree-2-year-deals-sharpe-minott |access-date=June 30, 2026 |website=espn.com |language=en}} ==National team career== Minott was born in [[Florida]] but plays for the Jamaican national team.{{cite web |last=Wheeler |first=Daniel |title=Josh Minott focuses on NBA dream |url=https://jamaica-gleaner.com/article/sports/20220327/josh-minott-focuses-nba-dream |website=[[The Gleaner]] |access-date=June 14, 2022 |date=March 27, 2022}} At the 2019 [[Centrobasket]] Under-17 Championship in Puerto Rico, he averaged 26 points, nine rebounds and 4.6 steals per game.{{cite web |title=Joshua Minott (JAM)'s profile – Centrobasket U17 Championship 2019 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/u17centrobasket/2019/player/Joshua-Minott |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=June 14, 2022}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular
